sources.quote: found more than 5 million Canadians aged 15 and older met criteria for a mood, anxiety or substance use disorder in the previous year
sources.title: The Daily — Study: Mental disorders and access to mental health care
sources.evidence: In 2022, more than 5 million people in Canada met the diagnostic criteria for a mood, anxiety or substance use disorder; over 5 million Canadians (18%) aged 15 and older met the diagnostic criteria for a mood, anxiety, or substance use disorder in the previous 12 months. Data from the Mental Health and Access to Care Survey collected March 17 to July 31, 2022.

sources.quote: Bill C-59 received royal assent on June 20, 2024 and added psychotherapy and counselling therapy to the exempt health care services in Schedule V of the federal Excise Tax Act
sources.title: Clarifying the new GST/HST exemption for psychotherapy and counselling therapy services - Canada.ca
sources.evidence: On June 20, 2024, Bill C-59 received royal assent. As a result, psychotherapists and counselling therapists were added to the list of health care practitioners whose professional services rendered to individuals are exempt from the GST/HST under section 7 of Part II of Schedule V.

sources.quote: psychotherapy in Ontario and counselling therapy in New Brunswick, Nova Scotia and Prince Edward Island
sources.title: Application of the GST/HST to Psychotherapy and Counselling Therapy Services - Canada.ca
sources.evidence: Psychotherapy services are regulated only in Ontario, while counselling therapy services are regulated only in New Brunswick, Nova Scotia, and Prince Edward Island. If a person practises in an unregulated province but has the qualifications equivalent to those necessary to be licensed in a regulated province, their services are considered psychotherapy or counselling therapy services for purposes of the GST/HST exemptions.

sources.quote: CRPO Professional Practice Standard 6.2 requires advertising to be truthful, accurate, factual and verifiable
sources.publisher: College of Registered Psychotherapists of Ontario
sources.title: Standard 6.2: Advertising
sources.evidence: Registrants ensure their advertising is truthful, accurate, factual, and verifiable. Testimonials from clients, former clients, or other persons regarding a registrants' practice are not permitted in advertising.

sources.quote: CRPO treats a star rating as a testimonial, so a registrant may not use one in advertising, and promoting a practice with a client testimonial is professional misconduct
sources.publisher: College of Registered Psychotherapists of Ontario
sources.title: Advertising: Testimonials, Endorsements, and Community Voting Awards - CRPO
sources.evidence: It is professional misconduct to use a testimonial by a client, former client or other person in the advertising of the registrant or their practice. Star ratings and community voting awards are considered a type of testimonial and are not permitted in advertising. Clients or others are not prevented from reviewing registrants on third party sites, provided the registrant does not request them to do so.

sources.quote: healthcare policy prohibits personalized advertising based on health conditions
sources.title: Health in personalized advertising - Advertising Policies Help
sources.evidence: Health content includes physical or mental health conditions, including diseases, sexual health, and chronic health conditions. Google doesn't allow personalized advertising based on personal hardships, which include health conditions, treatments, procedures; advertisers can't use advertiser-curated audiences for health-related sensitive content.

sources.quote: Meta prohibits ads implying a person's mental-health attributes
sources.title: Privacy Violations and Personal Attributes | Transparency Center
sources.evidence: Ads must not contain content that asserts or implies personal attributes. This includes direct or indirect assertions or implications about a person's physical or mental health (including medical conditions).

sources.quote: Health Professions and Occupations Act took effect on April 1, 2026
sources.title: Health Professions and Occupations Act (HPOA) - Province of British Columbia
sources.evidence: The Health Professions and Occupations Act (HPOA) replaced the Health Professions Act (HPA) on April 1, 2026. All professions that were designated under the HPA continue to be designated as professions under the HPOA.

flags.quote: and roughly half reported unmet needs
flags.issue: Statistics Canada's 2022 Mental Health and Access to Care Survey reports that more than 1 in 3 (36.6%) of those with a mood, anxiety or substance use disorder had unmet or partially met health and mental health care needs, not roughly half.
